technicalSkillsFramework.title: Technical Skills Proficiency Framework
technicalSkillsFramework.description: Proficiency level definitions for technical skills in risk, audit and control

0.label: No Experience
0.description: No exposure or experience in this area

1.label: Developing
1.description: Has tested, reviewed, or observed existing frameworks. External or support perspective. Works under supervision.

2.label: Proficient
2.description: Can operate, maintain, and improve established frameworks. Works independently within existing structures.

3.label: Advanced
3.description: Can implement and adapt frameworks using established methodologies. Builds and leads for specific contexts.

4.label: Expert
4.description: Can design from first principles. Creates methodologies. Leads enterprise-wide transformations. Recognised authority.

ownership.1: Tested or reviewed someone else's work
ownership.3: Built using established templates and methodologies
ownership.4: Designed the template or methodology itself

technicalSkills.name: Internal Controls (SOX/Non-SOX)
technicalSkills.description: Design, implementation, and testing of internal control frameworks including SOX compliance

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Has tested controls as external or internal auditor; documented findings and exceptions; understands control objectives, assertions, and testing methodologies
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Owns control testing program; maintains control documentation and evidence repository; tracks remediation; coordinates with external auditors; manages control owners
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented control frameworks in new areas or entities; designed test plans and control matrices; established control libraries; led remediation programs; SOX coordination
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built SOX environment from scratch; designed control taxonomy and methodology; led IPO or listing readiness; created control framework architecture; recognised as controls authority

interviewQuestions: Walk me through a control you tested - what was the objective, how did you test it, and what was the outcome?
Have you inherited a control environment or built one? Describe the difference in your experience.
Tell me about a time you identified a control gap. How did you remediate it?
What's your experience with SOX vs non-SOX controls? How do the requirements differ?

technicalSkills.name: Risk Appetite & Risk Framework
technicalSkills.description: Development and operationalisation of risk appetite statements and enterprise risk frameworks

proficiencyDefinitions.0: No risk appetite or framework experience
proficiencyDefinitions.1: Has reviewed risk appetite statements; understands concept of risk tolerance and capacity; tested adherence to risk limits; familiar with risk categories
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Operationalises existing risk appetite; reports on risk metrics and limit breaches; maintains risk framework documentation; escalates threshold breaches; supports risk committees
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Developed and cascaded risk appetite statements from board level to business units; translated qualitative appetite into quantitative limits; built risk reporting and dashboards
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Designed enterprise risk framework from first principles; created risk taxonomy and appetite methodology; authored board-level risk appetite statements; built risk function from scratch

interviewQuestions: How would you explain risk appetite vs risk tolerance to a business stakeholder?
Describe how you've seen risk appetite cascade from board level to operational limits.
Have you ever drafted a risk appetite statement? Walk me through the process.
What's the difference between maintaining a risk framework and building one?

technicalSkills.name: Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA)
technicalSkills.description: Design and facilitation of RCSA processes and risk identification methodologies

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Has participated in RCSA workshops as contributor; understands risk identification and rating process; contributed to risk registers; familiar with inherent vs residual risk
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Facilitates RCSA sessions with business areas; maintains and updates risk registers; coordinates risk ratings with control owners; produces RCSA reports; challenges assessments
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented RCSA methodology in new business areas; designed workshop templates and facilitation guides; trained RCSA facilitators; built risk libraries and taxonomies
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Designed RCSA framework from scratch; created inherent and residual rating scales and methodology; led enterprise-wide RCSA rollout; authored RCSA policy and standards

interviewQuestions: What's your role typically been in RCSA workshops - facilitator, contributor, or designer?
How do you challenge a business area that consistently rates their risks as low?
Have you ever had to implement RCSA in an area that didn't have it before?
What makes a good risk rating scale? Have you ever designed one?

technicalSkills.name: Policy & Procedure Development
technicalSkills.description: Creation and maintenance of policy frameworks, policies, standards, and procedures

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Has reviewed policies for compliance; tested adherence to policy requirements; understands policy hierarchy (policy, standard, procedure); identified policy gaps
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Maintains existing policies through annual review cycles; coordinates stakeholder input; tracks policy exceptions; manages minor updates and version control
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Drafted and implemented new policies end-to-end; managed stakeholder consultation and approval governance; created supporting procedures and standards; trained staff on new policies
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Designed enterprise policy framework architecture; created policy governance model and hierarchy; authored board-level policies; built policy management function and tooling

interviewQuestions: What's the difference between a policy, standard, and procedure? Give examples from your experience.
Have you written a policy from scratch or mainly maintained existing ones?
Walk me through how you'd get a new policy approved in an organisation.
How do you handle policy exceptions? What governance have you put around them?

technicalSkills.name: Regulatory Change Management
technicalSkills.description: Monitoring, assessing, and implementing regulatory changes and compliance programs

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Aware of key regulations affecting the business; supported regulatory examinations; understands regulatory expectations; monitored for regulatory updates
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Monitors regulatory horizon for relevant changes; assesses impact on policies and processes; maintains regulatory inventory and mapping; tracks compliance status; BAU regulatory reporting
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Led regulatory change implementation programs; conducted gap assessments against new requirements; managed remediation projects; prepared regulatory submissions and responses
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Designed enterprise regulatory change framework; built horizon scanning and impact assessment methodology; led strategic regulatory engagement; established compliance function

interviewQuestions: What regulations are you most familiar with? How did you stay current with changes?
Describe a regulatory change you had to implement. What was your role?
Have you ever conducted a gap assessment against a new regulation?
What's the difference between monitoring regulations and implementing regulatory change?

technicalSkills.name: Audit Planning & Execution
technicalSkills.description: Planning, execution, and reporting of internal audit engagements

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Supported audit engagements; performed testing under supervision; documented workpapers; understands audit lifecycle and methodology; conducted walkthroughs
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Plans and executes audits independently; writes findings, recommendations, and reports; manages auditee relationships; performs risk assessments for audit planning
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Designs audit programs and testing approaches; leads complex or integrated audits; develops audit methodology improvements; coaches and reviews junior auditors' work
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built audit methodology and function; strategic annual audit planning; CAE-level board and committee reporting; led audit transformation; designs audit quality framework

interviewQuestions: Walk me through an audit you led from planning to final report.
How do you determine what to test in an audit? What's your approach to scoping?
Have you ever designed an audit program or methodology, or worked within existing ones?
Tell me about a difficult finding you had to deliver. How did you handle it?

technicalSkills.name: Third Party Risk Management (TPRM)
technicalSkills.description: Assessment and ongoing management of vendor and third-party risks

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Supported vendor due diligence assessments; completed risk questionnaires; understands vendor risk categories; familiar with vendor lifecycle stages
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Conducts vendor risk assessments independently; maintains vendor inventory and tiering; coordinates ongoing monitoring and periodic reviews; escalates vendor issues
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented TPRM program in new areas; designed assessment methodology and questionnaires; created vendor tiering criteria; built vendor oversight and governance processes
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built TPRM function from scratch; designed enterprise-wide framework; created vendor risk taxonomy and methodology; regulatory-grade TPRM architecture; strategic vendor governance

interviewQuestions: How do you determine which vendors are high risk vs low risk?
Have you designed a TPRM program or worked within an existing one?
What does ongoing vendor monitoring look like in your experience?
Tell me about a vendor issue you identified and how you managed it.

technicalSkills.name: Operational Resilience & Business Continuity
technicalSkills.description: Business continuity planning, disaster recovery, and operational resilience frameworks

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Participated in BC testing and exercises; aware of recovery plans and RTOs/RPOs; understands Business Impact Analysis concepts; supported incident response
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Maintains BC and DR plans; coordinates testing exercises and documents results; updates plans based on organisational changes; supports crisis management
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented BC or resilience program; conducted Business Impact Analyses; designed recovery strategies; led scenario testing programs; built playbooks
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built operational resilience framework from scratch; designed impact tolerance methodology; led regulatory submissions; enterprise-wide resilience architecture; crisis management design

interviewQuestions: What's your experience with BC testing? Have you observed or designed the tests?
Explain the difference between RTO and RPO. How have you applied these concepts?
Have you conducted a Business Impact Analysis? Walk me through your approach.
What's operational resilience and how does it differ from traditional BC?

technicalSkills.name: Data Analytics for Risk & Audit
technicalSkills.description: Use of data analytics, automation, and technology in risk and audit functions

proficiencyDefinitions.0: No analytics experience in risk/audit context
proficiencyDefinitions.1: Uses pre-built dashboards and reports; interprets data outputs; understands data sources; basic Excel and BI tool user; can identify data quality issues
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Builds reports and analyses; writes SQL queries or uses analytics tools (ACL, IDEA, Power BI); creates dashboards; identifies anomalies and exceptions through data
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implements analytics programs for continuous monitoring; automates control testing; designs KRI frameworks with data feeds; builds exception reporting
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Designs analytics strategy for risk/audit function; builds data infrastructure and pipelines; implements advanced techniques (AI/ML); leads analytics transformation

interviewQuestions: What analytics tools have you used in risk or audit work?
Have you automated any testing or monitoring through data analytics?
Tell me about insights you've derived from data that you wouldn't have found manually.
What's the difference between using analytics and building an analytics capability?

technicalSkills.name: Issue & Action Management
technicalSkills.description: Identification, tracking, and remediation of audit findings, risk issues, and control deficiencies

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Documented findings and issues; understands issue lifecycle and severity ratings; supported remediation tracking; familiar with root cause concepts
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Manages issue inventory and aging; tracks remediation progress with action owners; validates issue closures; reports on issue metrics; escalates overdue items
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented issue management program; designed issue tracking methodology and severity criteria; conducts root cause analysis; established escalation frameworks
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built enterprise issue management framework; designed governance model and reporting; thematic analysis across issue population; board-level issue reporting; built tooling

interviewQuestions: How do you determine if an issue should be rated high, medium, or low?
What's your approach to validating that an issue has been properly remediated?
Have you ever conducted root cause analysis on recurring issues?
Describe the issue management governance you've worked with or created.

technicalSkills.name: Fraud Risk Management
technicalSkills.description: Fraud risk assessment, prevention, detection, and investigation frameworks

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Aware of fraud risk concepts and red flags; supported fraud risk assessments; understands fraud triangle; familiar with anti-fraud controls
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Conducts fraud risk assessments; maintains fraud risk register; monitors fraud indicators; supports investigations; implements anti-fraud controls
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented fraud risk management program; designed fraud risk assessment methodology; built detection analytics; established investigation protocols
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built enterprise fraud risk framework; designed fraud prevention strategy; created fraud risk taxonomy; led fraud function; expert witness or regulatory engagement

interviewQuestions: Explain the fraud triangle and how you've applied it in risk assessment.
Have you been involved in a fraud investigation? What was your role?
What fraud detection techniques or analytics have you used?
Describe a fraud prevention control you've implemented or improved.

technicalSkills.name: Model Risk Management
technicalSkills.description: Governance, validation, and oversight of models used in decision-making

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Aware of model risk concepts; understands why models need validation; familiar with model inventory concepts; supported model documentation
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Maintains model inventory; coordinates model validations; tracks model issues and limitations; monitors model performance; supports model governance
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Conducts model validations; implements model risk framework in new areas; designs validation methodology; builds model monitoring and reporting
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built model risk management function; designed enterprise model governance framework; created model tiering and validation methodology; regulatory model submissions

interviewQuestions: What types of models have you worked with from a risk perspective?
Have you validated a model? What was your approach?
What makes a model high risk vs low risk in your view?
Describe the model governance framework you've worked within or created.

technicalSkills.name: Regulatory Reporting
technicalSkills.description: Preparation and submission of regulatory returns and compliance reporting

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Supported regulatory report preparation; understands reporting requirements; familiar with regulatory deadlines; performed data validation checks
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Prepares regulatory returns; coordinates data gathering across functions; manages submission calendar; liaises with regulators on queries; maintains reporting procedures
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented new regulatory reporting requirements; designed reporting processes and controls; built reconciliation frameworks; led reporting remediation programs
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built regulatory reporting function; designed enterprise reporting architecture; strategic regulatory engagement on reporting matters; reporting transformation lead

interviewQuestions: What regulatory reports have you prepared or contributed to?
How do you ensure accuracy in regulatory reporting?
Have you implemented a new regulatory report? What challenges did you face?
Describe the controls around regulatory reporting in your experience.

technicalSkills.name: Corporate Governance Frameworks
technicalSkills.description: Design and operation of governance structures, committees, and oversight mechanisms

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Understands governance concepts; familiar with committee structures; supported board or committee reporting; aware of three lines model
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Supports committee operations; prepares papers and minutes; maintains governance calendars; tracks actions; coordinates between governance forums
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Designed committee terms of reference; implemented governance frameworks in new areas; built reporting packs; established escalation pathways
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built enterprise governance architecture; designed three lines model implementation; created board and committee framework; governance transformation lead

interviewQuestions: Explain the three lines model. How have you seen it applied?
What governance committees have you supported or reported into?
Have you designed terms of reference for a committee or governance forum?
What makes governance effective vs a tick-box exercise?

technicalSkills.name: IT General Controls (ITGCs)
technicalSkills.description: Assessment and testing of IT general controls including access, change management, and operations

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Has tested ITGCs (access controls, change management); understands ITGC categories; documented control gaps; familiar with IT control objectives
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Owns ITGC testing program; maintains IT control matrices; coordinates with IT teams; tracks IT remediation; understands IT infrastructure and applications
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented ITGC frameworks; designed IT control testing programs; led IT audit or SOX IT workstreams; built IT risk assessment methodology
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built IT control environment from scratch; designed ITGC framework and taxonomy; led IT transformation from control perspective; IT SOX implementation lead

interviewQuestions: Walk me through the main ITGC categories and give examples of controls in each.
How do you test access controls? What are common issues you've found?
Have you implemented IT controls or mainly tested existing ones?
What's the relationship between ITGCs and application controls?

technicalSkills.name: Data Privacy & Protection
technicalSkills.description: Data protection compliance, privacy frameworks, and information governance

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Aware of data protection regulations (GDPR, etc.); understands personal data concepts; supported privacy impact assessments; familiar with data subject rights
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Conducts privacy impact assessments; maintains data inventories; handles data subject requests; supports privacy compliance monitoring; coordinates with DPO
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented privacy program; designed DPIA methodology; built data mapping and inventory processes; led privacy remediation programs; created privacy controls
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built data privacy function; designed enterprise privacy framework; led GDPR or equivalent implementation; created privacy-by-design methodology; DPO-level accountability

interviewQuestions: What data protection regulations have you worked with?
Have you conducted a Data Protection Impact Assessment? Walk me through it.
Describe your experience with data subject rights requests.
What's the difference between privacy compliance and building a privacy program?

technicalSkills.name: AML & Financial Crime
technicalSkills.description: Anti-money laundering, sanctions, and financial crime prevention and detection

proficiencyDefinitions.0: No AML or financial crime experience
proficiencyDefinitions.1: Understands AML concepts and red flags; familiar with KYC requirements; aware of sanctions screening; supported AML audits or reviews
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Conducts customer due diligence; investigates transaction alerts; maintains AML procedures; prepares SARs; supports sanctions screening
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented AML programs; designed transaction monitoring rules; built KYC frameworks; led AML remediation; created financial crime risk assessments
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built financial crime function; designed enterprise AML framework; regulatory engagement on AML matters; led AML transformation; MLRO-level accountability

interviewQuestions: Explain the three lines of defence in an AML context.
What transaction monitoring experience do you have?
Have you filed a SAR? What was the process?
Describe an AML program you've implemented or improved.

technicalSkills.name: Cyber Security Risk
technicalSkills.description: Assessment and management of cyber security risks and controls

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Aware of cyber threats and vulnerabilities; understands basic security controls; supported cyber risk assessments; familiar with security frameworks (NIST, ISO27001)
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Conducts cyber risk assessments; evaluates security controls; monitors cyber risk metrics; coordinates with security teams; maintains cyber risk register
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented cyber risk programs; designed security risk assessment methodology; built cyber KRIs; led security control implementations; cyber audit experience
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built cyber risk function; designed enterprise cyber risk framework; strategic security engagement; CISO advisory; led cyber transformation programs

interviewQuestions: What cyber security frameworks are you familiar with?
How do you assess cyber risk differently from other operational risks?
Describe a cyber control gap you identified and how it was remediated.
What's the relationship between cyber security and cyber risk management?

technicalSkills.name: Conduct Risk Management
technicalSkills.description: Identification and management of conduct risk and customer outcome monitoring

proficiencyDefinitions.1: Understands conduct risk concepts; aware of treating customers fairly principles; familiar with conduct regulations; supported conduct risk assessments
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Monitors conduct risk indicators; assesses customer outcomes; maintains conduct risk framework; coordinates conduct MI; supports product governance
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Implemented conduct risk programs; designed conduct risk assessment methodology; built customer outcome testing; led product governance frameworks
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built conduct risk function; designed enterprise conduct framework; regulatory engagement on conduct matters; led conduct transformation; board-level conduct reporting

interviewQuestions: What does treating customers fairly mean in practice?
How do you measure conduct risk? What indicators have you used?
Describe a conduct risk issue you identified or addressed.
Have you implemented product governance or customer outcome testing?

technicalSkills.name: Scenario Analysis & Stress Testing
technicalSkills.description: Design and execution of risk scenarios and stress testing programs

proficiencyDefinitions.0: No scenario analysis or stress testing experience
proficiencyDefinitions.1: Participated in scenario workshops; understands scenario analysis concepts; familiar with stress testing purposes; contributed to scenario narratives
proficiencyDefinitions.2: Facilitates scenario analysis sessions; documents scenarios and impacts; coordinates stress testing data; produces scenario reports; maintains scenario library
proficiencyDefinitions.3: Designed scenario analysis methodology; built stress testing frameworks; led scenario selection and calibration; implemented reverse stress testing
proficiencyDefinitions.4: Built enterprise scenario and stress testing capability; designed methodology for regulatory stress tests; strategic scenario design; board-level stress test reporting

interviewQuestions: What's the difference between scenario analysis and stress testing?
Have you designed scenarios or worked with pre-defined ones?
How do you calibrate the severity of a stress scenario?
Describe a stress testing exercise you were involved in.

questions: Did you test/review it or build it?
Did you inherit the framework or create it?
Were you working from templates or designing the templates?
Was this one area/process or enterprise-wide?
Did you operate within methodology or define the methodology?
Were you the executor or the architect?

developing: Familiar with concepts but limited hands-on
Worked on single controls or processes

overClaimingIndicators: 'I was involved in' often indicates Level 1-2
'I designed from scratch' or 'I built the function' indicates Level 4
